findings.problem: This diff undoes the previous commit (e11187e, 'use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape'). It goes back to passing autoescape=True as an extra keyword through Jinja2Templates(directory=..., **env_options). The installed Starlette (0.52.1, starlette/templating.py:92-96) still accepts that path but marks it deprecated: importing triggarr.web.routes raises 'DeprecationWarning: Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead.' I confirmed this by running the import with -W error::DeprecationWarning. pyproject.toml lists fastapi and jinja2 with no version pin, so whether autoescaping is configured now depends on whatever Starlette version gets installed. The old code set autoescape=True directly on its own jinja2.Environment, so it held on any version. If a later Starlette removes **env_options, the app fails at import with a TypeError (startup abort). If a future version stops honoring the option, templates render user-controlled content unescaped (script injection). Today escaping still works because Starlette's _create_env also defaults autoescape to True, but that is a library default, not this code's guarantee. Any test run with warnings set to errors will also fail.

findings.problem: This diff reverts commit e11187e ('fix: use preconfigured jinja2.Environment for autoescape'), whose own message states: 'Starlette removed the **env_options passthrough in Jinja2Templates, breaking autoescape=True on newer versions.' That commit replaced `Jinja2Templates(directory=..., autoescape=True)` with a manually constructed `jinja2.Environment(loader=..., autoescape=True)` passed via `env=`, which Starlette applies unconditionally regardless of library version. This diff undoes that and goes back to `Jinja2Templates(directory=str(TEMPLATES_DIR), autoescape=True)`, routing `autoescape=True` back through Starlette's `**env_options` passthrough. Reading the installed starlette/templating.py (v0.52.1) confirms this path still works today, but it is explicitly marked deprecated there ('Extra environment options are deprecated. Use a preconfigured jinja2.Environment instead.', triggering a DeprecationWarning) and the project's own git history documents a prior Starlette release where this exact passthrough was dropped, silently falling back to jinja2's un-overridden Environment defaults. pyproject.toml pins fastapi/jinja2 with no upper bound, so a routine uv sync/lock refresh can pull a Starlette release that reproduces the exact regression this project already hit and fixed once.
findings.title: Reverts unconditional autoescape Environment, making stored-XSS protection dependent on a deprecated Starlette passthrough
findings.why_it_matters: Templates in triggarr/templates/settings.html render user-controlled config values (e.g. {{ inst.missing_tag }}, {{ inst.cutoff_tag }}, {{ inst.url }}) with no | safe and no manual HTML-escaping, relying entirely on Jinja2 autoescape. Verified in triggarr/web/routes.py (lines 452-453): missing_tag/cutoff_tag are stored with only .strip() applied -- no character allowlist -- and validate_arr_url (triggarr/web/validation.py) checks scheme/host but not quote or angle-bracket characters in the raw URL string that gets persisted and re-rendered. If autoescape silently reverts to Jinja2's default (effectively off, since no select_autoescape/explicit True is set on the fallback Environment) because a future Starlette release drops the env_options passthrough -- exactly as already happened once per this repo's own commit log -- an attacker who can reach the settings form (or a value synced from an untrusted *arr instance) could inject "><script>...</script> via missing_tag/cutoff_tag/url and achieve stored XSS in the admin settings page.
